cases.question: What happens if I fail more than 75% of my units?
cases.review_reason: The scholastic-delinquency table on Handbook page 35 is OCR-garbled. The readable cells say 75% or more / nine academic units or more → Dismissal from the College (not allowed to enroll), and 100% → Permanent disqualification from the University. Confirm against the PDF table.
cases.proposed_reference_answer:
The LSPU Student Handbook 2021 retention policy uses two slightly different failure thresholds.

Section 4.3 states that any student who fails in more than 75% of the total academic units enrolled shall be subject for dismissal from the College. An incomplete grade is not included in the computation of earned units. Section 4.3 also states that this shall not apply to students who receive final grades in only nine academic units.

The scholastic-delinquency table on the following page lists 75% or more, when the student is enrolled in nine academic units or more, as Dismissal from the College (not allowed to enroll). Failing 100% is listed separately as Permanent disqualification from the University, which is not the same as dismissal from the College.

The nine-unit language therefore appears in two contexts: as an exemption in Section 4.3 for students who receive final grades in only nine academic units, and as an enrollment condition in the table (nine academic units or more) for the 75% or more dismissal row.

Because Section 4.3 says “more than 75%” and the table says “75% or more,” these pages do not resolve the exact-75% case. Confirm the applicable rule with the Registrar.

cases.question: What is honorable dismissal for a student?
cases.review_reason: Definition and conditions are in consecutive Handbook chunks of Article 12, page 47. Confirm wording against the PDF (extraction has split words such as 'with drawal').
cases.proposed_reference_answer: The Student Handbook (Undergraduate Academic Policies > Article 12 > Honorable Dismissal, page 47) defines Honorable Dismissal as voluntary withdrawal from the college/university with the consent of the Registrar. A student in good standing who wants to withdraw presents a written petition to the Registrar signed by the parent/s or guardian/s; if granted, Honorable Dismissal is issued. All indebtedness to the university must be settled first. The statement indicates good standing as to character and conduct. A student granted honorable dismissal may not be readmitted. A student who leaves because of suspension, dropping, or expulsion for disciplinary action is not entitled to Honorable Dismissal.
